title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Criminals used AI-generated videos and deepfakes to impersonate a real immigration attorney and create hundreds of fake social media profiles offering fraudulent legal services to immigrants. The scam operated across multiple platforms, with the impersonators directing victims through WhatsApp and collecting payments via digital money transfer apps for services that were never provided. This is an impersonation attack enabled by generative AI tools, deployed at scale with no authentication mechanism between the fake accounts and the real attorney's identity.

The failure occurred in the social media platforms' account verification and content moderation systems. The scammers were able to create thousands of accounts bearing the attorney's name and likeness without triggering the kind of identity checks that might have caught the impersonation earlier. The scam was discovered only when victims contacted the real attorney's office, meaning the platforms' existing safeguards did not detect the abuse. It is not established whether the scammers used AI systems specifically designed for fraud or repurposed legitimate generative tools.

What remains unclear is whether the social media platforms had any obligation to verify the identity of users offering professional services, or whether such verification would have been technically or operationally feasible at the scale these platforms operate.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of a major AI-based scam operation targeting immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos using his likeness to promote fraudulent immigration services, including false claims of securing US residency for $2,200 payments. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, and the situation has dramatically escalated in recent months. His firm hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake accounts across multiple platforms, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram.

The scammers typically use social media videos to direct victims to contact numbers through WhatsApp, where they send phony contracts and request payment through digital money transfer apps like Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Other fraudulent videos feature fake testimonials from supposed former clients. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scams. He is warning immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and to be cautious of promises requiring immediate payment.
